deep.reconstruction:
The page is an outline of lecture notes on elementary mechanics (pendulum, falling motion, circular motion, energy, impact). It contains no extended computation. The implicit content is reconstructed below; anything beyond the explicit words is mine.

(1) Bohnenberger's reversion pendulum (Bohnenbergersches Reversionspendel). Take a rigid body of mass m, centre of mass G, moment of inertia I_G = m*kappa^2 about G. Suspended from an axis at distance h from G, it swings as a compound pendulum. [mine] Its moment of inertia about the axis is I_O = m*(kappa^2 + h^2). Its swing time (19th-century 'Schwingungsdauer' = one swing, i.e. a half-period) for small amplitudes is T = pi*sqrt(I_O/(m*g*h)) = pi*sqrt(L/g). Here L = h + kappa^2/h is the length of the equivalent mathematical pendulum.

[mine] For a given T, and hence a given L, the distance h satisfies h^2 - L*h + kappa^2 = 0. This has two roots h1, h2 with h1 + h2 = L and h1*h2 = kappa^2. Each root can be taken on either side of G. That gives the explicit statement: '4 axes of equal swing time, symmetric with respect to the centre of mass'.

The second explicit statement follows. The distance between two axes not placed symmetrically (h1 on one side of G, h2 on the other) is h1 + h2 = L, the length of the mathematical pendulum. This is the principle of Bohnenberger's (1811) and Kater's (1817) reversible pendulum: L is measured as a distance between knife edges, without knowing G or kappa.

(2) 'Swing time and the whole course of the swing ... valid for arbitrary arcs.' Read together with the next line ('Cycloid / tautochrone swing'), this refers to the cycloidal pendulum. Its period is independent of amplitude and equals pi*sqrt(L/g) exactly, with L = 4a for a cycloid generated by a circle of radius a.

(3) The formula line is written roughly as 'k = (Schwingungsdauer)^2', read as a formula for the acceleration of gravity (Fallgeschwindigkeit / Beschleunigung). [mine] From T = pi*sqrt(L/g) one gets g = L*(pi/T)^2, and per unit length g = (pi/T)^2. The intended content is presumably that the gravitational constant follows from the measured swing time and L.

(4) 'Most important application: clocks.' Then fragmentary remarks: the pendulum lets weight act only through its own load; pendulum motion and free fall are related ('verwandt'), since both are governed by the same constant g.

(5) Remaining outline headings:
- motion of oscillation of weights;
- circular motion (Kreis-/Rundbewegung);
- application of the law of conservation of 'Kräfte' (vis viva / energy) to the laws of motion;
- laws of impact (Stoßgesetze).
The next page continues with impact, distinguishing elastic and inelastic collisions. It notes that the motion of the common centre of mass is unchanged by the collision.
errors: The formula line as it appears reads only '(Schwingungsdauer)^2' with no length factor and an unclear numerator. The correct relation is g = pi^2*L/T^2 (T = half-period). As written it is either an abbreviated note (g per unit pendulum length) or a slip; the illegibility prevents a firm judgement.
No other substantive errors. The reversible-pendulum statements (four axes of equal period symmetric about G; distance of a non-symmetric pair = equivalent length) are correct.

results.what: Axes of equal period of a compound pendulum: four, symmetric about the centre of mass; distance between a non-symmetric pair equals the equivalent simple-pendulum length
results.modern_name: Reversible (Kater/Bohnenberger) pendulum; conjugacy of centres of suspension and oscillation
results.usually_credited_to: Huygens (1673, conjugate centres); Bohnenberger (1811); Kater (1817); also Prony

results.what: Determination of gravity from swing time: g = pi^2 L / T^2
Cycloidal pendulum: period independent of amplitude
Outline: pendulum clocks, relation of pendulum and free fall, circular motion, conservation of vis viva, impact laws

deep.surprise_reason: These are lecture or study notes on textbook mechanics: the reversible pendulum, the cycloidal pendulum, g from the pendulum period, and a syllabus of energy and impact. All of it was standard by the early 19th century. Nothing here is original or attributable as a new result.

checkable.asserts: The two suspension distances with equal period sum to the equivalent length L
Distances h and kappa^2/h give the same equivalent length L = h + kappa^2/h, hence the same period
g = pi^2 L / T^2 for swing (half-period) T = pi*sqrt(L/g)
Cycloidal pendulum (s'' = -g s/(4a)) has swing time pi*sqrt(4a/g), independent of amplitude s0 (should simplify to 0)

transcription_corrections: 'symmetrisch zu Schwerpunkt' is more likely 'symmetrisch zu dem Schwerpunkt'.
'für beliebige Körper (z. B. Erd-Masse)' is more plausibly 'für beliebige Bogen (z. B. ...)', referring to amplitude independence.
The formula line appears as 'k = (Schwingungsdauer)^2' with no clearly written pi; the inserted pi/ is conjectural.
'Cycloiden Schwingung' could alternatively be 'Tautochrone Schwingung'; the reading is uncertain.
'Uhren (Chronometer)': the parenthetical is uncertain, possibly 'Uhren (Ganggesetz)' or similar.
'Anwendung d. Ges. d. Erh. d. Kräfte' reading is uncertain (possibly 'Anwendung d. allg. ...'); the sense of conservation of vis viva fits the next page.
